% note: Post hoc sample counts. Format not ok: the sample's official format status (the marking rule with Deviation~2) is not ok; the kinds are listed under not-ok format statuses. Format ok but wrong: format ok, answer wrong. Right: the official answer is right; every right sample is format ok, because the official rule scores a sample whose format is not ok as wrong. The three counts add up to the samples (both checked when the table is built).
% note: The post hoc analysis calls the format-not-ok samples ``unparseable'', but on chains such a sample can still carry a readable, even right, final answer. Scored on the final answer alone, Study~1's chains reach 27.97\% against the official 22.00\% (an exploratory setting). On pieces the final answer is the whole answer, so the two scores coincide (checked against Study~1's stamped final-answer scoring); no other chain row has a stamped final-answer accuracy.
% note: Accuracy on format-ok samples (the post hoc analysis calls it ``accuracy on parseable tries'') is the right answers among the format-ok samples divided by the format-ok samples. It is conditional on format and is not a whole-answer accuracy.
% note: Labels. In Study~1, Haiku, thinking off, is one of the pre-registered exploratory settings, so its accuracy and 95\% interval are exploratory values, read from Study~1's pre-specified table of every setup's results. The format columns (samples, format ok, format compliance and the not-ok statuses) are pre-specified descriptive in both studies (the pre-registered format rules). Study~1b's accuracy and interval are pre-specified descriptive. The columns marked post hoc are a post hoc descriptive recount of the per-sample scores; the recount's samples, format ok, statuses and accuracy on all samples agree with the locked values (checked when the table is built).
% note: Study~1 and Study~1b used different puzzle sets and different runs; set side by side, their rows are a reading across studies: our reading, not a test.
% note: (exact): the bootstrap interval collapsed to one value; the exact (Clopper--Pearson) 95\% interval over puzzles replaces it (post hoc presentation).
